title: Manifold learning tests electrolyte categories against paired clinical measurements
summary: A neural ECG model classified potassium, calcium and magnesium categories using paired laboratory measurements in MIMIC-IV. In the study cohort of8599 patients, potassium macro-F1 was0.61, calcium0.50 and magnesium0.40. This is retrospective clinical-reference evaluation, not a validated replacement for laboratory testing.
ai_technology: MINN; ResNet18; learned manifold-source network; metadata fusion
organization: Harvard University; Duke Kunshan University; Duke University

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual learned model Methods, clinical/physical-reference evaluation and limitations

evidence.tested: The study paired18037 ECG recordings with nearby serum measurements and used patient-level time-based partitions. A learned source network and ECG encoder were jointly fitted with a graph residual objective.
evidence.unknown: One-center archived data, imbalanced categories and up-to-one-hour pairing differences limit transportability. Medication/demographic metadata contribute to prediction, especially for calcium/magnesium; the result is not ECG-only inference. Preprocessing can truncate late waveform content. No prospective independent clinical validation, diagnostic deployment or patient benefit was established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned waveform features, task-aware graph-source inference and metadata fusion enable the source-specific laboratory-referenced category classification.
